title: Why is there a tiny hole in your airplane window?
question: Why does an airplane window have a tiny hole in it?
answer: The hole in the middle pane equalises pressure so the outer pane carries the cabin load and the middle pane stays as an unstressed backup; it also lets moisture out so the window does not fog.

c1.text: A passenger window has three panes: inner, middle and outer.
sources: Time, 'This Is Why There Are Holes in Airplane Windows', https://time.com/3903109/airplane-window-holes
Gizmodo, 'Why Is There a Hole in Airplane Windows?', https://gizmodo.com/why-is-there-a-hole-in-airplane-windows-1703660371

c2.text: The hole is in the middle pane; it equalises pressure so the outer pane carries the load and the middle pane is a backup.

c3.text: Air through the hole lets moisture out of the gap, which keeps the window from fogging.
sources: BGR, 'Those Tiny Holes In Airplane Windows Have An Important Purpose', https://bgr.com/2155765/why-airplane-windows-have-tiny-holes/

scenes.say: There's a hole in your plane window.

image.subject: an oval passenger aircraft cabin window with rounded corners seen from inside the cabin
image.show: a tiny round hole near the bottom edge of the window, small but clearly visible

scenes.say: Look closely next time you fly. A tiny hole, near the bottom. On purpose.

image.subject: the lower edge of an aircraft cabin window
image.show: a pin-sized round hole drilled through a clear acrylic pane, fine hatching around it

scenes.say: A plane window isn't one sheet. It's three panes: inner, middle and outer.

image.subject: an aircraft cabin window assembly
image.show: three separate curved acrylic panes in a row with air gaps between them, set in the fuselage wall

scenes.say: The hole is in the middle pane. It lets cabin air into the gap, so the pressure on both sides of the middle pane stays equal.

image.subject: a cross-section of two aircraft window panes
image.show: air flow lines passing through a small hole in the inner of the two panes into the gap between them, equal arrows on both sides

scenes.say: So the outer pane carries the load. The middle one waits, unstressed, as a backup if the outer pane ever fails.
And the air moving through the hole takes moisture with it, so the window doesn't fog up or frost over.

image.subject: an aircraft cabin window at high altitude
image.show: a clear pane with faint frost crystals only at the outer edge, a thin stream of air through a tiny hole

scenes.say: One tiny hole, two jobs. Nothing is ordinary when you understand how it works.
